queer_characters.name: Brandon Shaw
queer_characters.notes: Original stage play explicitly portrays Brandon and Phillip as a homosexual couple; screenwriter Arthur Laurents ('I thought it was apparent') and actor Farley Granger confirmed the characters were gay. In the film the murderers' villainy and queerness are intertwined, a harmful predatory-queer pattern, though a product of Hays Code-era censorship.

queer_characters.name: Phillip Morgan
queer_characters.notes: Depicted with Brandon as a live-in homosexual couple in the source play; cast and screenwriter acknowledged the gay subtext. The film ties their queerness to their murderous villainy, reflecting a harmful trope under censorship constraints.

contributor_notes: Source text notes queerness is subtext obscured by the Hays Code but confirmed by screenwriter Arthur Laurents and actor Farley Granger — hence 'confirmed-by-creator' rather than 'inferred.' A landmark example of censorship-era queer-coding where villainy and queerness are intertwined. Maintainer may wish to consider whether 'historical-context' better fits rep_quality than 'harmful.' No creator identities stated in source, so queer_creators left empty despite named contributors.
